issues.failure_explanation: The introduction says block scrambling is necessary to keep the (0,e,d) structure and that digitwise scrambling fails to do so. But a digitwise nested scramble in base b, read on blocks of e_j digits, is itself a nested scramble in base b^{e_j}. Each block is mapped by a bijection depending only on earlier blocks, and different prefixes use disjoint independent families of digit permutations. By Proposition prop:added-1 it therefore preserves equidistribution in base (b^{e_1},...,b^{e_d}), i.e. the (0,e,d) property, with probability 1. What usual scrambling lacks is two-fold uniformity in base b^{e_j}, which the mixed-base gain analysis needs; it does not lose structure preservation.

failure_location.quote: scrambling entire blocks of digits is the natural and necessary way to maintain this structure

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword: both scramblings preserve the (0,e,d) property. Coarse scrambling is needed so that the scramble is two-fold uniform in the mixed base, which makes the mixed-base gain-coefficient analysis applicable.
issues.overall_effect: The stated motivation and the first contribution misrepresent what distinguishes coarse scrambling. No formal result is affected.
issues.title: False claim that digitwise scrambling cannot preserve the (0,e,d) property
issues.why_classification: Only the motivational prose changes. All theorems and guarantees are unaffected.

let $\tilde{P}_n$ be its randomly scrambled version using a nested scramble with two-fold uniformity

issues.failure_explanation: A nested scramble is defined to use mutually independent permutations for all prefixes. In the block affine scramble, the permutation at block level k for prefix p is x -> D_k x + sum_{i<k} M_{k,i} p_i + Delta_k. The same D_k, M_{k,i} and Delta_k serve every prefix, so these permutations are dependent. For example, in base 2 with e=1 the shifts are affine in p, and the shifts at four prefixes summing to zero add to zero. Thus the lemma is false as stated, and its omitted proof by analogy with [Ma98, Ow03] cannot establish it: those standard affine scrambles are not nested scrambles in this sense either. Consequently Theorem thm:added-2, whose hypothesis is a nested scramble with two-fold uniformity, does not cover the proposed implementation.

failure_location.quote: is a nested scramble in base $\bsb$ and has two-fold uniformity

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either replace the independence requirement by the pairwise properties actually used, and prove that the variance formula (variance-gain) holds for block affine scrambles in mixed base (an analogue of Owen 2003), or restrict the theory to fully nested coarse scrambling.
issues.overall_effect: The variance formula and the gain-coefficient guarantees are not established for the block affine scramble, the only concrete coarse scrambling proposed and the one used in the experiments. They remain valid for fully nested coarse scrambling.
issues.title: Block affine matrix scramble is not a nested scramble under the paper's definition
issues.why_classification: Restoring coverage of the proposed method needs a contained but nontrivial new argument. The main theory is otherwise unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The union of the disjoint sets $L_{\bsl(u,\bsk')}$ over all $\bsk' \le \bsk$ covers exactly the set of all Walsh indices $\bsh$ where $h_j < b^{k_j+1}$ for all $j \in u$ and $h_j=0$ for $j \notin u$.

issues.failure_explanation: Here l_j = k'_j + 1 >= 1, so each L_{l(u,k')} forces h_j >= 1 for j in u. The union therefore misses Walsh indices with h_j = 0 for some j in u. The cell average tilde-beta_{u,u,k} contains f_emptyset and all components beta_{w,.} with w a proper subset of u. Counterexample: for u={1}, k=0, (eq:beta) gives beta_{u,0} = tilde-beta_{u,u,0} - f_emptyset, contradicting (beta2) whenever the mean is nonzero. The proof of lem:beta-basechange relies on (beta2). It also uses index -1 when k_j=0 and j is not in v; there the empty usual-base sum is 0 while tilde-beta^{(C)}_{u,v,k} is nonzero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (beta2) as tilde-beta_{u,u,k} = f_emptyset + sum over nonempty w subset of u and k'_w <= k_w of beta_{w,k'}, valid also for zero resolution. Then observe that lower-order terms cancel in the inclusion-exclusion over v in the base-change proof.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix identity is false, and the proof of the base-change lemma is invalid as written. The lemma's conclusion and the results built on it are true but are not established by the given argument.
issues.title: Identity (beta2) omits lower-order ANOVA terms; appendix set-union claim false
issues.why_classification: A short routine correction and cancellation step restores all stated results, with no loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: eq:C_def normalizes C by 1/n^2, so C <= 1. The lemma and its proof compute the raw pair count instead: for n=2 and m=1 the formula gives 4, while the definition gives 1. Separately, eq:Gtilda_def includes 1/n and eq:G_Gtilde adds another 1/n. When all points lie in distinct cells this yields G = 1/n, contradicting thm:mimic(i), the claimed value Gamma_u, and the MC normalization in (variance-gain). eq:Gtilda_formula is consistent with neither normalization. All later computations silently use the unnormalized double sum and count.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the 1/n from eq:Gtilda_def and the 1/n^2 from eq:C_def, so that tilde-G and C are unnormalized, consistent with eq:Gtilda_formula, the lemma and the proofs.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the stated gain values (1, 0, Gamma_u) and the variance formula are off by factors of n.
issues.title: Inconsistent normalizations of tilde-G and C versus the counting formula
issues.why_classification: A local normalization fix forced by the variance formula restores every claim unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Item (iv): take u={j}, k=0 (so k'=1) and n=b_j. Item (i) gives G_{u,k'}(b_j)=1, but item (ii) gives G_{u,k'}(b_j^2)=0, contradicting (iv). Item (v): take u={j}, k=0 and n=1. The left side G_{u,0}(b_j) is 0 by (ii), while G_{u,0}(1)=1 by (i). The cited Owen-Pan arguments support G_{u,k'}(nb_j)=G_{u,k}(n) and G_{u,k}(n prod_j b_j^{k_j})=G_{u,0}(n), not the statements given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (iv) by G_{u,k'}(n b_j) = G_{u,k}(n), and (v) by G_{u,k}(n prod_{j in u} b_j^{k_j}) = G_{u,0}(n).
issues.overall_effect: Two items of the general theorem are false as written. Later results use the correct forms implicitly.
issues.title: Scaling identities in Theorem items (iv) and (v) are false as stated
issues.why_classification: Correcting the statements is local, and no downstream conclusion changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It follows that the bound \eqref{eq:general_bound_coarse} has more terms

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's 0-based levels l_j, gains of a (t,m,d)-net vanish only when sum_j (l_j+1) <= m - t_u. Nonzero terms therefore satisfy sum_j l_j > m - t_u - |u|. As written, the bound omits the levels m - t_u - |u| < sum l_j <= m - t_u. This contradicts the source's own 1D formula for t=0, which includes l=m, and the e=1 case of cor:gain-0ed. With t_u = sum_j (e_j - 1), the correct dense bound has exactly the same index set as (general_bound_coarse). The claim that the coarse bound has more terms is therefore wrong, and the hypothetical t_u = sum_j e_j in thm:added-3 is unnecessary.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the index condition sum_j l_j > m - t_u - |u| in (general_bound_dense), and revise the 'more terms' comparison accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The coarse-versus-usual comparison in Section 4 is misstated. thm:added-3 remains true, since the coarse bound is still dominated.
issues.title: Quoted usual-scrambling bound drops terms (off by |u| in level index)
issues.why_classification: This is a local index correction. No theorem or rate is lost, and the comparison only becomes more favorable to coarse scrambling.
